item.title: Democrat Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom will win the election for U.S. Senate in Mississippi, The Associated Press projects.

item.title: At least 2 dead, multiple injured after building collapses in Brooklyn: Mayor
item.description: Multiple firefighters responded to the scene.

item.title: WATCH: ABC's Bob Woodruff's foundation honors wounded soldiers and their families
item.description: David Muir speaks with "The Resilient" – a band made up of wounded soldiers – backstage at Bob Woodruff's annual Stand Up for Heroes, raising millions for veterans and military families.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins historic Senate race in Mississippi
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom defeated Republican Senator Cindy Hyde-Smith in Mississippi after a final count on Wednesday, becoming the state's first Black US senator since Reconstruction. His narrow victory adds to the Democrats' midterm gains as President Donald Trump's party suffers a series of defeats.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV returns to second homeland Peru to a nationwide welcome
item.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Peru on Wednesday for the final leg of his South American tour, returning to the country where he spent more than two decades as a missionary and bishop. Thousands gathered to welcome him home as “Padre Robert”, with many hoping his visit will bring attention to poverty, crime and political instability.

item.title: Two killed in 'devastating' New York building collapse
item.description: At least two people have been killed after a "devastating" building collapse in Brooklyn, New York City's mayor has said.

item.title: Democrat Scott Colom wins Mississippi Senate race
item.description: Democrat Scott Colom has won election to the U.S. Senate in Mississippi, according to a race call by the Associated Press, defeating Republican Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith.

item.title: Nvidia preparing to oust CEO amid reports of a second affair
item.description: Nvidia is reportedly preparing to oust its CEO - after US media outlets claimed that Jensen Huang has had a second extramarital affair.

item.title: European leaders gather in Dublin under the shadow of hybrid threats
item.description: Ireland is mounting the largest security operation in its history as around 50 European leaders gather in Dublin this week amid growing concerns over hybrid attacks. The operation follows a wave of hoax bomb threats targeting airlines and media organisations across Europe, with Irish police reporting new incidents on Monday and Tuesday. FRANCE 24's Olivia Bizot reports.

item.title: Gadi Eisenkot unveils agenda to reverse Netanyahu’s policies
item.description: The bloc of Israeli prime ministerial hopeful Gadi Eisenkot introduced a series of bills at the start of the legislative session that target Benjamin Netanyahu and his policies. They include launching an official government-led inquiry into the Hamas-led Oct. 7, 2023, attacks, setting term limits on the position of prime minister and overturning changes the outgoing Netanyahu-led government made to limit the powers of the judiciary. FRANCE 24's Sharon Gaffney speaks with Rina Bassist, Editor at Al-Monitor.

item.title: Father of infant buried alive charged with attempted murder
item.description: The father of an 11-month-old boy rescued after being buried alive in a dog crate has been charged with attempted murder in South Carolina, police said.

item.title: Russia and Ukraine agree to major prisoner swap as peace talks end
item.description: Kyiv and Moscow on Wednesday agreed to a large-scale prisoner exchange as the final day of peace talks in Abu Dhabi came to an end, though neither side gave a concrete figure. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner will meet separately with Russian President Vladimir Putin and his Ukrainian counterpart Volodymyr Zelensky on Thursday.

item.title: Several Democrats missed the crucial Hegseth impeachment vote. Many blamed traffic
item.description: Eleven Dems missed the critical vote, squandering Hegseth's impeachment attempt.

item.title: Tshisekedi paves way for constitutional change
item.description: In tonight's edition, A new law expanding the conditions for a constitutional referendum has ignited political tensions in the DRC. Also, Kenya has officially declared the end of its latest Ebola outbreak. And at COP31, environmental advocates are warning against waste incineration, arguing that it risks locking African cities into expensive and polluting infrastructure.

item.title: Discharge petition on 2nd Epstein files bill secures 218 signatures
item.description: A discharge petition to force a vote on the Epstein Files Transparency Act II has amassed 218 signatures, teeing up additional floor action on the prospective bill.

item.title: Woman, 80, in critical condition after being set on fire
item.description: An 80-year-old woman set on fire outside her flat has been named by police.

item.title: General strike over housing brings out hundreds of thousands in Spain
item.description: Millions of workers in Spain shut down businesses and public transport on Wednesday, as part of the country's first general strike in 14 years. Following a peaceful march in Barcelona over soaring rents and property prices, and the rising cost of living, protesters smashed storefronts, set off small bonfires, burned bins and launched fireworks towards police. The unrest comes just weeks before snap elections, called by Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Mosque handed warning over 'inflammatory' sermons seeks legal advice
item.description: An Islamic centre that was given an official warning for hosting "inflammatory, divisive" sermons by the charities regulator is seeking legal advice.

item.title: Rare Marilyn Monroe photos from her final shoot to be auctioned
item.description: Prints from the personal collection of renowned photographer Bert Stern, including his celebrated series The Last Sitting of Marilyn Monroe, are set to be auctioned at Gros & Delettrez in Paris, marking the first such sale of Stern's private archives. At the heart of the Dec. 2 auction is The Last Sitting, a series of photographs taken in June and July 1962 at the Hotel Bel-Air in Los Angeles, just weeks before Monroe's death. FRANCE 24's Olivia Bizot reports.

item.title: France turns back Israeli settler representative upon arrival in Paris
item.description: French authorities forced Samaria Regional Council head Yossi Dagan to leave the country after he landed at a Paris airport last week, his office said in a statement on Wednesday. The French foreign ministry did not confirm his deportation, only saying that Dagan was banned from French territory due to his involvement in Israel's illegal settlements in the occupied West Bank.

item.title: RSF calls for release of French reporter Christophe Gleizes, detained in Algeria
item.description: After being detained for almost 500 days in Algeria, Christophe Gleizes is no closer to being freed. Those close to him, as well as his fellow sports journalists have campaigned tirelessly for his release with the affair even attracting the attention of Zinedine Zidane, manager of the French football team. FRANCE 24's Mark Owen speaks with Thibault Bruttin, Director General of Reporters Without Borders. He says that Gleizes has probably become "a token in a diplomatic game that we don't totally understand, that we don't totally master, up to the point where we are asking ourselves 'has he become a state hostage?'".

item.title: Rex Ryan surrenders in alleged hit-and-run that injured 2 pedestrians: Police
item.description: Former NFL head coach Rex Ryan surrendered in Nashville on Wednesday on six outstanding misdemeanor warrants, police said.

item.title: Biden says he wouldn't have run for a second term in 2024 if he knew he had cancer
item.description: Joe Biden says he didn't know he had cancer while he was president and wouldn't have sought a second term if he'd already been diagnosed

item.title: Why is gasoline suddenly under $4 a gallon?
item.description: The average price of a gallon of gasoline dipped below $4 this week for the first time in months. Does that mean more relief is coming for drivers?

item.title: General strike over housing brings out tens of thousands in Spain
item.description: Tens of thousands of protesters marched across Spain on Wednesday during a general strike over housing affordability and purchasing power just weeks before an early general election. Unions reported a significant response in some sectors in Spain's first nationwide 24-hour stoppage since 2012, but business leaders played down the participation. Braving heavy rain, tens of thousands of demonstrators marched through central Madrid carrying placards shaped like houses and chanting "We have no home" as they called for more affordable housing. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris reports from Madrid.

item.title: Undone by a honey trap? Nvidia's Jensen Huang at heart of China spy scandal
item.description: Turns out that the new masters of the universe are human, all too human. China accused of exploiting a vulnerability at the heart of the Silicon Valley giant that reigns supreme over two-thirds of the planet’s AI computing power production, the Nvidia co-founder tempted by the flesh. Jensen Huang admitting to an extramarital affair with Singapore-based Chinese tech CEO Alice Huang - no relation. She’s under scrutiny over the purchase of Nvidia state-of-the-art chips that may have been smuggled back to the mainland illegally. We’ll ask about the rise and possible fall of the Taiwan-born leather-clad AI world icon.

item.title: Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days after shootings
item.description: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for an annual Independence Day March, just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow that shook the country. The event is held each November 11 to commemorate the ending in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria. The event is a magnet for all shades of Poland's right wing -- from conservative-nationalists aligned with its Law and Justice (PiS) party to far-right and radical groups. FRANCE 24's Carys Garland reports.

item.title: Schools evacuated across Italy after bomb threats
item.description: Schools were evacuated across Italy on Wednesday following a series of hoax bomb threats, but Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni said there was no "concrete danger". Similar hoax threats were reported in schools in Britain and Ireland, which reportedly prompted some evacuations in Scotland. Meloni said she had called a government meeting with security and intelligence chiefs for Wednesday to discuss the threats. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.

item.title: The most hacked country in Europe? Why is France the target of so many cyberattacks
item.description: The “unprecedented” hacks of French supermarket refrigerators were the latest in a series of major cyberattacks that have made the country the most hacked in Europe, according to some analysts. Cyberattacks are on the rise globally, but why is France such a ready target?

item.title: Tens of thousands attend Polish nationalist march days afer shootings
item.description: Tens of thousands of Polish nationalist sympathisers gathered in Warsaw Wednesday for an annual Independence Day March, just days after a deadly shooting spree in Krakow that shook the country. The event is held each November 11 to commemorate the ending in 1918 of 123 years of partition by Russia, Prussia and Austria. While generally peaceful, some rallies in the pasthave been marred by clashes with police or counter-demonstrators. Philip Turle gives us his take.

item.title: Kennedy relatives join the fight against Trump's arch, alleging harm to JFK's grave
item.description: Nine members of the Kennedy family have joined the legal fight against Trump's D.C. arch, arguing it would disrupt views and cast shadows over their ancestors' graves at Arlington National Cemetery.

item.title: Tehran will strike US bases in Europe if used to attack Iran, security chief says
item.description: Iranian security chief Mohsen Rezaei said Wednesday that Tehran would attack US bases located in Europe if they were used to carry out bombing raids against the Islamic republic. The heavy defeat of US President Donald Trump's Republican Party in the midterm elections earlier this month seems to have pushed Washington to pull back its threats to carry out fresh strikes against Iran.
